senses.gloss: To grow steadily larger or stronger.
examples: Costs *mount* quickly once a project runs late.
Pressure *mounted* on the mayor to resign.
Evidence has been *mounting* for months.

senses.gloss: To get up onto a horse or a bicycle.
examples: She *mounted* the horse and rode toward the gate.
He *mounts* his bike and disappears down the hill.
*Mounting* a tall horse takes some practice.

senses.gloss: To organize and carry out something large, such as a campaign or an attack.
examples: The museum will *mount* a show of her early work.
The team *mounted* a comeback in the fourth quarter.
Neighbors are *mounting* a campaign against the new highway.

senses.gloss: To affect someone's feelings deeply.
examples: Stories like that always *move* me.
The ending *moved* her to tears.
We were deeply *moved* by his letter.

senses.gloss: To formally propose something at a meeting or in court.
examples: I *move* that we postpone the vote until Friday.
The defense *moved* to dismiss the charges.
A board member has *moved* for a recount.

senses.gloss: To find the total of one number added to itself a given number of times.
examples: *Multiply* the length by the width to get the area.
She *multiplied* six by seven in her head.
We were *multiplying* fractions all morning.

senses.gloss: To do something perfectly, in informal English.
examples: If you *nail* the interview, the job is yours.
She *nailed* her audition and got the part.
He has *nailed* the accent after months of practice.

senses.gloss: To catch someone and prove they are guilty, in informal English.
examples: Store security *nails* about one shoplifter a week.
The IRS finally *nailed* him for tax fraud.
He was *nailed* by a traffic camera on Fifth Street.

senses.gloss: To appoint someone officially to a job, a team, or an honor.
examples: The board will *name* a new chief executive on Monday.
They *named* her captain before the season started.
He was *named* to the All-Star team for the third time.

senses.gloss: To deal successfully with a complicated system or situation.
examples: It is hard to *navigate* the health insurance system alone.
She *navigated* the divorce with help from her sister.
We are still *navigating* the new tax rules.

senses.gloss: To fail to do something, usually without meaning to.
examples: Don't *neglect* to sign the last page.
He *neglected* to mention that he was married.
She had *neglected* to renew her passport.

senses.gloss: To get past or safely over something difficult.
examples: He *negotiates* the icy steps one at a time.
The truck barely *negotiated* the narrow bridge.
*Negotiating* that hairpin turn in the rain is frightening.

senses.gloss: To fit one thing neatly inside another.
senses.ru: вкладывать один в другой, вставлять внутрь
examples: The mixing bowls *nest* inside each other.
She *nested* the boxes to save room in the closet.
*Nesting* folders too deeply makes files hard to find.

senses.gloss: To catch a fish or an animal in a net.
examples: They *net* shrimp close to shore.
He *netted* a trout the size of his arm.
The crew has *netted* three tons this week.

senses.gloss: To earn an amount as profit after costs are taken out.
examples: The store *nets* about a thousand dollars a day.
The sale *netted* them forty thousand dollars.
He has *netted* a tidy profit on the rental.

senses.gloss: To meet people who may be useful to your career.
examples: She *networks* at every conference she attends.
He *networked* his way into the film business.
I spent the evening *networking* with other teachers.

senses.gloss: To cut a small V-shaped mark into something.
examples: *Notch* the edge so the rope will not slip.
He *notched* the stick once for every day.
The post had been *notched* to hold the beam.

senses.gloss: To pay attention to something and keep it in mind.
examples: Please *note* that the office closes at four.
She *noted* the change in his tone right away.
It should be *noted* that the data is incomplete.

senses.gloss: To gently encourage someone toward a decision.
examples: A reminder email *nudges* people to pay on time.
Her parents *nudged* her toward medical school.
He kept *nudging* me to apply for the job.

senses.gloss: To add up to a particular total.
examples: The staff now *number* fewer than twenty.
The crowd *numbered* about five thousand.
Protesters *numbering* in the thousands filled the square.

senses.gloss: To feed a baby milk from the breast.
examples: The puppies *nurse* every couple of hours.
She *nursed* both of her children for a year.
He fell asleep while *nursing*.

senses.gloss: To hold on to a feeling for a long time.
examples: She still *nurses* a quiet hope of moving back.
He *nursed* a grudge against his brother for years.
They have been *nursing* that grievance since the merger.

senses.gloss: To obey a law or rule, or to keep a holiday or custom.
examples: Drivers must *observe* the speed limit in a school zone.
Her family *observed* Passover at her grandmother's house.
A minute of silence was *observed* before the game.

senses.gloss: To block a road, a pipe, or a view.
examples: Please do not *obstruct* the doorway.
A fallen tree *obstructed* the road for hours.
Our view of the stage was *obstructed* by a pillar.

senses.gloss: To live or work in a place, or to fill a space or a period of time.
examples: Her family *occupies* the top two floors.
The meeting *occupied* the whole morning.
Every seat in the theater was *occupied*.

senses.gloss: To keep someone busy.
examples: A box of crayons will *occupy* the kids for an hour.
She *occupied* herself with a crossword while she waited.
He kept the toddler *occupied* while I cooked.

senses.gloss: To lead an official ceremony, especially a wedding.
examples: Who is going to *officiate* at the wedding?
A retired judge *officiated* their marriage.
Her uncle has *officiated* at three family weddings.

senses.gloss: To show a quality very strongly.
examples: He *oozes* confidence in every interview.
The old hotel *oozed* charm.
She walked in *oozing* self-assurance.

senses.gloss: To move a door, lid, or container so that it is no longer closed.
examples: *Open* the window; it is hot in here.
She *opened* the letter with a kitchen knife.
The door had been *opened* from the inside.

senses.gloss: To begin business for the day, or to become available to the public.
examples: The bakery *opens* at six in the morning.
They *opened* a second store downtown last spring.
A new clinic is *opening* on Main Street.

senses.gloss: To start something official, such as an account or an investigation.
examples: I want to *open* a savings account.
Police *opened* an investigation into the fire.
The committee has *opened* hearings on the crash.

senses.gloss: To perform surgery on a patient.
examples: The doctors decided to *operate* immediately.
They *operated* on his knee twice in one year.
She has never been *operated* on before.

senses.gloss: To ask a restaurant or a store to supply something.
examples: She always *orders* her coffee black.
We *ordered* a pizza and watched the game.
The parts have been *ordered* and should arrive Friday.

senses.gloss: To arrange things in a particular sequence.
examples: *Order* the names alphabetically, please.
The photos are *ordered* by date.
He spent an hour *ordering* his notes before the exam.

senses.gloss: To form a labor union, or to bring workers together to act as one.
examples: The warehouse workers voted to *organize*.
They *organized* three stores last year.
Baristas have been *organizing* since 2021.

senses.gloss: To turn or place something so that it faces a particular direction.
examples: *Orient* the map so that north is at the top.
He *oriented* the antenna toward the tower.
The house is *oriented* to catch the morning sun.

senses.gloss: To draw or mark the outer edge of a shape.
examples: *Outline* the shape first, then fill it in.
She *outlined* the letters in black ink.
His figure was *outlined* against the window.

senses.gloss: To put too much electricity into a battery.
examples: Don't *overcharge* the battery or it will swell.
He *overcharged* the cells and ruined the pack.
The batteries had been *overcharged* overnight.

senses.gloss: To have a view over something from above.
senses.ru: выходить на (о виде из окна), возвышаться над
examples: Our room *overlooks* the harbor.
The cabin *overlooked* a small lake.
We ate on a terrace *overlooking* the river.

senses.gloss: Of a taste or smell, to be so strong that it hides everything else.
examples: Too much garlic *overpowers* the sauce.
Her perfume *overpowered* the whole elevator.
The chili was *overpowering* everything else in the bowl.

senses.gloss: To officially reverse a court decision or a law.
examples: Lawyers hope to *overturn* the ban this fall.
An appeals court *overturned* the conviction.
The ruling was *overturned* after new evidence appeared.

senses.gloss: To defeat someone completely by greater force or numbers.
examples: A larger force will *overwhelm* the defenders.
The troops *overwhelmed* the outpost in an hour.
The small garrison was quickly *overwhelmed*.

senses.gloss: To feel that you should thank or repay someone for what they did.
examples: I *owe* you an apology.
She *owes* her whole career to that teacher.
We *owed* them a favor, so we said yes.

senses.gloss: To admit a mistake and accept responsibility for it.
senses.ru: признавать (вину, ошибку), брать ответственность на себя
examples: A good manager *owns* her mistakes.
He *owned* the error and apologized to the team.
She has *owned* her part in the failure.

senses.gloss: To control your speed or effort so that you do not run out of energy.
examples: *Pace* yourself; it is a long day.
She *paced* the race perfectly and won.
He is *pacing* himself through a heavy semester.

senses.gloss: To fill a place completely with people.
examples: Thousands *pack* the square every New Year's Eve.
Fans *packed* the stadium two hours before kickoff.
The hall was *packed* with worried parents.

senses.gloss: To describe someone or something in a particular way with words.
examples: The report *paints* a grim picture of the city's finances.
The prosecutor *painted* him as a con artist.
Both sides have *painted* the deal as a victory.
